statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-75806 ("Unauthenticated and Undersized DTLS 1.2 AEAD Record Causes DoS", Low): the TLS and DTLS 1.2 record layer passed an AEAD-protected record to the cipher before checking that it was long enough to hold the explicit IV and the authentication tag, so a single unauthenticated datagram with a shorter encrypted fragment, routed to an established DTLS 1.2 association that uses an AEAD cipher suite, makes OpenSSL raise a fatal internal_error alert and tear the association down without the attacker knowing any key material; in TLS 1.2 the same record only changes the alert sent. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/3a4589d015a9049d47b66f186cf50a8711343a1d, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.9. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, DSA-6531-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-75806. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-75806. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The fix adds that length check to tls1_cipher() in libssl. In the libssl symbol table (shipped debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build), tls1_cipher() is 2984 bytes on amd64 and 2700 bytes on arm64 in every build before the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, and 2995 and 2680 bytes in that build and every later build, FIPS builds included. Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
